pr_title: Optimize Ordinal.EqualsIgnoreCase_Vector with AVX2 and AVX512
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-runtime See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/92497 Currently, `str1.Equals(str2, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` is only accelerated with `Vector128`, this PR adds `Vector256` and `Vector512` via `ISimdVector` abstraction - the best part that there is no code duplication. ```cs public class Benchmarks { static readonly string s1 = @"C:\prj\runtime\src\coreclr\System.Private.CoreLib\System.Private.CoreLib.csproj"; static readonly string s2 = @"C:\prj\runtime\src\coreclr\System.Private.CoreLib\system.Private.CoreLib.csproj"; [Benchmark] public bool EqualsIgnoreCase() { return s1.Equals(s2, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase); } } ``` | Method | Toolchain | Mean | Error | StdDev | Ratio | |----------------- |---------------------- |----------:|---------:|----------:|------:| | EqualsIgnoreCase | Core_Root\corerun.exe | 10.470 ns | 4.530 ns | 0.2483 ns | 1.00 | | EqualsIgnoreCase | Core_Root_PR\corerun.exe | **5.502 ns** | 4.186 ns | 0.2295 ns | 0.53 |
Author: EgorBo
Assignees: EgorBo
Labels: `area-System.Runtime`
Milestone: -

@stephentoub @tannergooding PTAL, some notes:
1) I copied parts of `Ascii.EqualsIgnoreCase` here, I can't just invoke `Ascii.EqualsIgnoreCase` because we need to fallback to ICU in case of non-ascii, while `Ascii.EqualsIgnoreCase` just bails out. I'll think of how I can unify them separately - didn't want to regress `Ascii.EqualsIgnoreCase` by adding more conditional logic in it.
2) Trailing elements are now handled with SIMD (used to be scalar) so all benchmarks for Length=8 (chars) and higher show improvements.

Had to replace == with Equals due to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/93174
Ping, also cc @adamsitnik @MihaZupan who authored/contributed Ascii.cs where I copied this code from

issue_context.title: Add AVX/AVX512 to Ordinal.EqualsIgnoreCase
issue_context.body:
`Ordinal.EqualsIgnoreCase` currently has a SIMDified path only for `Vector128`: `EqualsIgnoreCase_Vector128` and since we're observing this call in traces on hot path for one of our 1P customers, it should makes sense to add AVX and AVX2 here. For that, we need to re-use existing `Ascii.EqualsIgnoreCase` API that already does it, the problem that that API gives up on on non-ASCII input while we want to know the exact position where we gave up in order to switch to the slow fallback - we need to modify that API to return it.

review_comments:
This might noticeably regress comparisons for `length < TVector.Count` when AVX512 fully lights up, and a lot of string comparisons might fall under such a scenario (< 32 chars).

Naturally, this poses a challenge of expressing TVector vectorized core, with TVector / 2 (e.g. AVX512 -> AVX2) fallback to ensure ~10-30 character strings are compared quickly.

I'm not sure what would the good catch-all solution for such problem look like given how most vectorized loops are currently implemented in CoreLib, but it might become more of a problem in the future, so I wanted to highlight this.

p.s.: bonus headache points for also considering alignment which is now back on the menu with AVX512 :D quick research of Rust's stdlib and some garden variety C++ SIMD libraries shows they usually do [scalar head handler for alignment] -> [simd body] -> [scalar remainder handler] (but I assume the requirement to do this is additionally warranted by having to support platforms which require such loads to always be aligned). Whether this is worth it or not to expend LOCs on in .NET is a good question, it's mostly a problem for operations on string sub-slices which may be completely misaligned.
The implementation can be updated to handle trailing elements via SIMD too
Data alignment is worth doing but it's sadly quite verbose to do. It's especially beneficial to do for string opts because chars in string objects are only 4-byte aligned.

> Data alignment is worth doing but it's sadly quite verbose to do. It's especially beneficial to do for string opts because chars in string objects are only 4-byte aligned.

Would we pin to guarantee we're keeping alignment for the whole loop or would we just align at the start and hope the GC doesn't move stuff if we'd be adding that to SIMD loops in .Net?

You will have to make it part of the public ISimdVector interface to work (like, a separate API accepting char), that's why I didn't even try 🙂

Not specific to just this PR, but would the expectation be that the different `ISimdVector` impl variants are inlined into the caller?
Or should we be spamming them with aggressive inlining / counting on PGO to decide to avoid the extra calls into the correct helper?
I think it depends on a case? in this case the original function was not inlineable too. Hopefully, the time budget problem will be less relevant in .net 9.0
